notes: Replaced route-matchers-conjunction with root-route-matcher-restriction to avoid repeating b2's matcher-conjunction fact.

cards.statement: For float gauge g, sum by(job)(g) merges series sharing job despite differences in instance.
cards.explanation: by(job) retains job as the grouping label; without(instance) retains labels other than instance.

cards.statement: For native histogram vector h, PromQL count(h) adds the observation counts stored in h.
cards.explanation: count(h) counts native histogram elements in the instant vector, regardless of their observation counts.
cards.misconception: count() sums histogram observation totals.

cards.statement: For float vector v, PromQL topk(3, v) retains the original labels of its selected series.
cards.explanation: topk() returns selected input elements with their labels, preserving information such as instance.

cards.statement: For native histogram vector h, PromQL max(h) selects the histogram with the largest observation count.
cards.explanation: max() ignores native histogram samples and flags their removal with an info-level annotation.
cards.misconception: max() ranks native histogram samples by their observation counts.

cards.statement: For mixed float and native histogram inputs, PromQL sum(v) keeps the float subtotal for the same output group.
cards.explanation: sum() removes an output group mixing float and native histogram samples, with a warning annotation.
cards.misconception: sum() silently omits native histograms while keeping the group's float subtotal.

cards.statement: For float per-instance latency means m, PromQL avg(m) weights busy instances more heavily.
cards.explanation: avg() averages the input series values; weighting instance means by request volume needs an explicit calculation.
cards.misconception: avg() weights per-instance mean values by their originating request volume.

cards.statement: For float vector v, PromQL v > 5 filters v while retaining surviving sample values by default.
cards.explanation: For float vectors, v > 5 returns original values passing the comparison; bool produces truth values.

cards.statement: PromQL can match float vectors on(job) when job values agree and both sides have one series per job.
cards.explanation: on(job) compares job values and disregards other labels when establishing matches.

cards.statement: PromQL can multiply float vectors with group_left when both sides have multiple series per match key.
cards.explanation: group_left needs one right-side series per match key for its many-to-one arithmetic join.
cards.misconception: group_left enables many-to-many arithmetic joins.

cards.statement: For float vectors a and b, PromQL a + b supplies zero for a missing match by default.
cards.explanation: PromQL omits vector elements whose matching labels have no partner on the other side.
cards.misconception: Unmatched vector arithmetic uses an implicit zero.

cards.statement: For matching float vectors, PromQL multiplication drops __name__ even with on(__name__, job).
cards.explanation: Arithmetic vector results lose the metric name even when the matching clause explicitly includes __name__.

cards.statement: For float vectors, PromQL and selects matching left-side series even when the right-side value is zero.
cards.explanation: The and operator tests matching series presence, so a zero-valued right-side sample still qualifies.

cards.statement: For stored float gauge g, PromQL accepts sum(g offset 5m) with offset inside the aggregation.
cards.explanation: PromQL attaches offset to the selector inside sum(); putting it after the complete aggregation is invalid.

cards.statement: PromQL's offset -5m shifts selection five minutes earlier than the evaluation time.
cards.explanation: With offset -5m, PromQL selects relative to a point five minutes ahead of its evaluation time.
cards.misconception: Negative offsets select older data.

cards.statement: In a range query, g @ 1609746000 fixes the selector's reference time across query steps.
cards.explanation: Numeric @ pins a selector's reference timestamp while the surrounding range query advances through its evaluation times.

cards.statement: For float gauge g, (g * 2)[30m:1m] forms a range vector from repeated evaluations of g * 2.
cards.explanation: Subquery brackets with a colon collect repeated evaluations of an instant-vector expression over the specified duration.

cards.statement: PromQL uses scrape_interval as the resolution of a subquery that omits its resolution.
cards.explanation: Prometheus uses the global evaluation interval for a subquery whose resolution is omitted.
cards.misconception: An omitted subquery resolution follows scrape cadence.

cards.statement: Prometheus 3.15.0 includes a sample exactly five minutes old in g[5m] at its evaluation time.
cards.explanation: Prometheus 3 treats the left range boundary as open, so g[5m] excludes a sample exactly five minutes before its reference time.
cards.misconception: The left boundary belongs to a selected range.

cards.statement: Prometheus aligns range-query evaluation timestamps to the timestamps of stored samples.
cards.explanation: Prometheus schedules evaluation times independently of the stored samples' timestamps.
cards.misconception: Query evaluation timestamps follow stored sample timestamps.

cards.statement: For a live series, PromQL selects its newest sample inside lookback in an instant selector.
cards.explanation: Lookback lets an instant selector reuse a recent stored value when the evaluation instant falls between samples.

cards.statement: PromQL instant selectors return zero-valued samples for series marked stale.
cards.explanation: PromQL's instant selectors omit stale series instead of returning a numeric zero.
cards.misconception: Stale series remain present with a zero value.

cards.statement: Prometheus immediately marks missing exporter-timestamped series stale with track_timestamps_staleness: false.
cards.explanation: Prometheus skips disappearance-based stale markers for honored exporter timestamps when track_timestamps_staleness is false.
cards.misconception: Honored exporter-timestamped series get immediate stale markers when they disappear.
cards.appliesTo: Prometheus 3.15.0 with honor_timestamps: true and track_timestamps_staleness: false

cards.statement: PromQL absent(v) returns an empty vector when float vector v contains a zero-valued element.
cards.explanation: absent() tests whether its input vector has elements. A zero-valued sample still supplies an element.

cards.statement: PromQL absent_over_time(g[10m]) returns a one-element vector valued 1 when g's selected range is empty.
cards.explanation: The function looks across the selected duration, so a sample anywhere in that range suppresses its empty-range signal.

cards.statement: Prometheus loads rule files named by the rule_files field in its main configuration.
cards.explanation: rule_files tells Prometheus which files contain the recording and alerting rules to evaluate.

cards.statement: Prometheus starts a group's next scheduled evaluation while its previous evaluation is running.
cards.explanation: Prometheus skips scheduled group iterations while the preceding evaluation remains unfinished.
cards.misconception: Slow group evaluations overlap their next scheduled iteration.

cards.statement: Prometheus evaluates ordinary rules within a group sequentially in their configured order.
cards.explanation: Within a group, the usual evaluation order follows the rule list, permitting later rules to use earlier recorded results.

cards.statement: Prometheus derives a recording rule's output metric name from its expr field.
cards.explanation: The record field sets the output metric name; expr determines the values the recording rule evaluates.
cards.misconception: A recording rule's expression chooses the output metric name.

cards.statement: promtool check rules validates local rule files while the Prometheus server is stopped.
cards.explanation: promtool check rules parses local rule files; validation works before any running server loads those rules.

cards.statement: promtool test rules evaluates its test cases against metrics stored in a running Prometheus server.
cards.explanation: Rule tests use input_series fixtures and expected outputs supplied in test files.
cards.misconception: Rule tests read their metric input from a running server.

cards.statement: Prometheus treats a zero-valued element returned by an alert expression as an inactive alert.
cards.explanation: An alert expression activates instances for its returned label sets, including elements with a zero value.
cards.misconception: Alert expression elements need positive values to activate instances.

cards.statement: Prometheus uses for to delay firing until an alert stays active through the configured duration.
cards.explanation: The for timer tracks one alert instance's continuous active period; a disappearance during pending resets that wait.

cards.statement: Prometheus keeps a firing alert active after its condition clears for its configured keep_firing_for duration.
cards.explanation: keep_firing_for extends the firing period beyond loss of the triggering condition, reducing brief false resolutions.

cards.statement: Prometheus starts a new alert instance when a templated annotation changes while its labels stay unchanged.
cards.explanation: Prometheus identifies alert instances by their labels and updates annotations on the existing instance.
cards.misconception: Annotation values participate in alert-instance identity.

cards.statement: Prometheus stores an alert expression's current value in its corresponding ALERTS synthetic series.
cards.explanation: Prometheus gives ALERTS a sample value of 1 while the labeled alert state is active.
cards.misconception: The ALERTS series preserves the alert expression's numeric value.

cards.statement: Prometheus periodically resends firing alert information to its configured Alertmanager instances.
cards.explanation: Prometheus refreshes firing alert information at Alertmanager while the alert continues firing.

cards.statement: Alertmanager deduplicates an alert group's notifications separately for different receiver integrations.
cards.explanation: Alertmanager keys sent-notification history by group and receiver integration, so delivery to one destination does not mark another as notified.

cards.statement: With group_by: [cluster] in one route, Alertmanager splits same-cluster alerts into groups by instance.
cards.explanation: For a given route, group_by: [cluster] puts same-cluster alerts together even when their instance labels differ.
cards.misconception: group_by adds its labels to implicit grouping by instance.

cards.statement: For newly firing alerts, Alertmanager uses group_wait before a new group's initial notification.
cards.explanation: group_wait gives recently firing alerts time to collect into the initial notification for a new group.

cards.statement: Alertmanager restarts the group_interval countdown whenever an alert joins an existing group.
cards.explanation: group_interval drives recurring checks for group changes; a new arrival joins the batch for a scheduled check.
cards.misconception: New alert arrivals debounce the existing group's notification timer.

cards.statement: Alertmanager uses repeat_interval to schedule reminders for a firing group whose alert set stays unchanged.
cards.explanation: repeat_interval governs reminders after a successful notification when the group's firing and resolved alert sets stay the same.

cards.statement: Alertmanager discards an alert when it reaches a route whose children fail to match it.
cards.explanation: When its children leave an alert unmatched, Alertmanager handles that alert using the current route's receiver and settings.
cards.misconception: Alerts that miss child routes fall out of the routing tree.

cards.statement: An Alertmanager child route inherits its parent's receiver when it leaves receiver unset.
cards.explanation: A child route's omitted receiver uses its parent's receiver setting.

cards.statement: Alertmanager accepts severity and team matchers on its root route to select the alerts entering the routing tree.
cards.explanation: Alertmanager's root route matches incoming alerts unconditionally; configuration validation rejects matchers on that route.
cards.misconception: The root route accepts label matchers just like child routes.

cards.statement: With continue: true on a matching child, Alertmanager explores later siblings after that child's subtree.
cards.explanation: continue controls traversal of subsequent sibling routes after a matching child returns, including a child with its own routing subtree.

cards.statement: Alertmanager inhibits a matching target when a firing matching source differs on labels listed in equal.
cards.explanation: An inhibition rule needs source and target alerts whose label values listed in equal agree.
cards.misconception: Inhibition works across differing equal-label values.

cards.statement: Alertmanager applies an active service="api" silence to matching alerts received after the silence starts.
cards.explanation: Alertmanager checks incoming alert labels against active silence matchers, including alerts received after the silence was created.

cards.statement: An Alertmanager silence changes a matching alert from firing to inactive in Prometheus.
cards.explanation: A silence suppresses notifications in Alertmanager. Prometheus continues evaluating its rule and determining the alert's state.
cards.misconception: Notification suppression clears Prometheus's firing alert state.
